title: While in edit mode, ESC key doesn't do anything if the pointer is over a Panel widget
line: Pressing Escape in edit mode now leaves edit mode even while the pointer is over a panel widget.
explanation: While the Panel Settings dialog is open, hovering a panel widget shows a popup (Remove/Configure/Show Alternatives) that activates itself and takes keyboard focus. Its content item never had focus, so the Escape handler added in 2025 never ran, and it only tried to close the popup anyway; Escape therefore did nothing. The content item now gets focus and Escape leaves edit mode, which also closes the panel settings.

containments/panel: leave edit mode on Escape over a widget handle

The popup shown over a hovered widget in edit mode takes keyboard focus,

review.text: The root cause is right and making Escape over a panel widget's edit-mode handle popup exit edit mode directly is consistent with the rest of the panel. However, setting focus: true directly on mainItem (a MouseArea, not a FocusScope) shares a focus scope with its descendant panelSpacerWidth SpinBox, whose dynamic focus binding permanently clears mainItem.focus to false after hovering a fixed-size Panel Spacer, re-breaking Escape on subsequent widgets.
changes: Wrap the MouseArea in a FocusScope (or make mainItem a FocusScope with focus: true and Keys.onEscapePressed containing the MouseArea) so child items like panelSpacerWidth or focused buttons/switches cannot clear the container's own focus in tooltip's root focus scope.
Verify that pressing Escape over a regular widget still exits edit mode after first hovering a non-expanding Panel Spacer (where panelSpacerWidth takes and releases focus).

reviews.text: Correct diagnosis of the case Nate still reproduced in c5: the widget handle popup calls requestActivate() and takes keyboard focus, but its mainItem never had focus, so the Escape handler from c1fc05b5 never ran, and it only closed the popup anyway. Giving the mainItem focus and leaving edit mode on Escape is a minimal two-line QML fix in the right file, and the before/after screenshots and regression notes (dialog Escape, panel handle Escape, Configure button) back it up. One Escape over a widget now closes Panel Settings and exits edit mode together, unlike the two-step Escape elsewhere, but that is an acceptable trade-off and is what the reporter wanted in c4.
